With the article τὰ μάλιστα [the most], about which L. Dindorf spoke in Thes. vol. 5 p. 537, Sept. 1077: μηδ᾽ ἀλλοδαπῶν κύματι φωτῶν κατακλυσθῆναι τὰ μάλιστα [nor to be overwhelmed by the wave of foreign men, the most], where L. Dindorf correctly reads κατακλυσθῆν [to be overwhelmed], deleting τὰ μάλιστα [the most], as the verse responding to this one, 1071, demands.

Harpocration μαλκίομεν [we are numb]: Demosthenes in the 9th Philippic says “μένομεν καὶ μαλακιζόμεθα [we remain and are soft].” In some manuscripts is written μάλκίομεν [we are numb], which means to shudder at the rump. Aeschylus (fr. 330) "ἕλα, δίωκ᾿ ἀκμῆτι [come, pursue with unwearied] (thus Hermann for ἐλαδίω κεκμῆτι) μαλκίων ποδί [with numb foot]." words perhaps spoken about Philoctetes, as Hermann conjectures. The verb is corrupted in various ways in the manuscripts, about which see Thes. vol. 5 p. 541.
